referents.why: Possessive his on hand (w7), masculine singular. Aaron is the subject of cl1, who stretches out the hand; no other candidate holds it.
referents.category: possessive in the clause's own subject

referents.why: Possessive his on staff (w10), masculine singular. The command named it your staff, addressed to Aaron, and cl1 has Aaron stretching it out.
referents.category: possessive in the clause's own subject

referents.why: Plural 3mp implied subject of 'they did so', a fulfilment report with no named subject. The command chain ran from the LORD through Moses to Aaron, so the plural is the pair Moses and Aaron; the acts that follow are Aaron's.
referents.category: implied subject of a fulfilment report

referents.why: Implied 3ms subject of 'he struck'. The nearest agreeing referent is Aaron, the subject of cl1 and the one the strike command was given to.
referents.category: implied subject in a narrative clause

links.why: cl4 is a closing summary of the gnat result (qatal, no waw), not the next event after cl0. The wayyiqtol line runs cl0 to cl3; cl4 does not follow on it.
links.category: summary clause wrongly placed on the narrative line

links.why: wayyiqtol cl1 continues the narrative line after the report cl0.
wayyiqtol cl2 is the next act after the stretching out.
wayyiqtol cl3 follows the striking on the narrative line.
Pro-form 'they did so' (3mp, not negated, no named subject) after the command chain. It points at the nearest preceding command, the strike; the stretch-out command is carried out by cl1 and cl2.
links.category: fulfilment report of an earlier command

links.why: Narrative clause repeating the verb of the stretch-out command.
Narrative clause repeating the verb of the strike command.
Repeats the verb of the command's effect (it will become gnats), so it fulfils the effect.
The stretching out is the detail of the report they did so.
The striking is the detail of the report they did so.
All the dust, throughout Egypt, is the detail of the gnats that came from it.
The striking is the act whose outcome is the gnats. The sense requires the causal link, not only sequence.

groups.why: cl1 and cl2 are two acts in a row by one agent, Aaron. cl2 states its subject only in the verb.
The stretch-out command in the earlier verse, then the same act reported as done.
groups.category: command then report of its act

groups.why: The strike command in the earlier verse, then the same act reported as done.
groups.category: command then report of its act

none_fit.what: A summary clause restating the effect for the whole land. No link type marks a restatement; elaborates is used instead.

cant_tell.what: Whether Moses is included in the plural they of cl0s
cant_tell.why: The clauses that follow have Aaron alone as doer, but the report is plural. The composite is chosen on the morphology and the command chain; the text does not say whether Moses joined in.

cant_tell.what: The members of the imperative groups Exo.8.12#imp2 and imp3
cant_tell.why: The earlier verse lists them by id without members, so it cannot be confirmed which command clauses they hold. The fulfils links point at the clauses themselves.
